articles.title: HOW TO LAUGH (AND WIN) WITH NEXT GEN
articles.summary: Gen Z and Gen Alpha use humor as a way to build identity and navigate culture. Snapchat's study found 74% are more likely to consider buying from funny brands, while 83% pay more attention to them. Brands should understand the context behind internet humor before joining trends. The best brand content adds to existing conversations through irony and formats audiences can remix and share.

articles.title: WHY ADVERTISERS SHOULDN'T GET TOO EXCITED ABOUT MICRODRAMAS
articles.summary: Microdramas attract strong audience attention but current platform economics limit the advertising opportunity. ReelShort users now spend 35.7 minutes a day on the app, yet the platforms rely on subscriptions and in-app purchases because standard video ads take up too much of a two-minute episode to work well. Brands can still use the format through branded entertainment, as shown by Nivea Malaysia and KFC, but those campaigns require high-quality storytelling that is difficult and expensive to repeat at scale. Watch the format for future growth, but treat it as a niche content strategy instead of a new advertising channel.

articles.title: WHY NO ONE'S CLICKING “SEND VIA DM”
articles.summary: Low “send via DM” activity usually signals content isn't built to be shared. Make posts more “sendable” by delivering standalone value someone would pass along. Bring back high-signal formats like original data, strong insights, or visual breakdowns that feel useful. Narrow the POV to focus on core audience needs instead of covering too many topics. Layer in deeper formats like video to increase engagement and make ideas easier to understand and share.

articles.title: LINKEDIN IS CRACKING DOWN ON AI SLOP. HERE'S WHAT THAT MEANS FOR YOUR STRATEGY
articles.summary: The AI writing tools LinkedIn embedded in its own product helped produce the flood of generic content the platform is now suppressing. Posts flagged as AI slop keep their visibility to direct connections but lose recommendation-engine distribution, so higher posting frequency now consumes slots without delivering reach. The line is whether a post contains something only its author or their organization could provide, a client outcome, a first-party data point, or a specific internal observation. AI used for research and drafting is fine. AI used for the thinking is what gets caught.

articles.title: OPENAI BRINGS PRODUCT CAROUSELS TO CHATGPT ADS
articles.summary: OpenAI is rolling out a product carousel format for ChatGPT ads, letting multiple products from a single retailer appear in one placement rather than the single-product unit that's run for five months. The system pulls product data directly from retailer feeds, similar to Google's Shopping feed, and OpenAI's own platform decides whether to serve a single ad or a carousel rather than leaving that choice to advertisers. The mechanics are already built to support competing retailers in the same carousel.

articles.title: WISPR FLOW LAUNCHES A GRANOLA-STYLED MEETING NOTETAKER
articles.summary: Wispr Flow launched a Mac notetaker that captures meetings using system audio without joining the call. It transcribes conversations in real time, cleans up notes, generates summaries and action items, and lets users query past meetings with AI. The move expands Wispr Flow beyond dictation into meeting intelligence.

articles.title: STUDY: DOES TOPICAL FOCUS MAKE YOUR BRAND MORE VISIBLE?
articles.summary: Owning a topic helps AI search recommend your brand, but broad content only works when you build deep authority in each category instead of spreading shallow coverage. The study found brands earned citations in 50% of distant categories but mentions in only 25%, which suggests AI will cite broad expertise but reserve recommendations for brands that consistently cover core topics. Repeated visibility across related categories improved future brand mentions, while shallow presence across many categories reduced them. The effect varies by industry, so finance and real estate brands can test adjacent category expansion using citations as an early signal, while legal and healthcare brands need repeat brand mentions before treating a category as established.

articles.title: COPYWRITING FRIDAY: STEVE JOBS LAUNCHES THE IPHONE
articles.summary: Steve Jobs made the original iPhone launch memorable because it followed a clear sequence that built curiosity, solved a problem, answered objections, and proved value one step at a time. The presentation delayed the reveal, framed existing smartphones as frustrating, and turned every feature into a customer benefit instead of listing specifications. Jobs also used specific proof points such as a 160 pixels per inch display and Apple reaching its 100 millionth iPod to make claims feel credible. Strong product marketing works best when each message has one purpose, every claim has proof, and every page or presentation moves the audience to the next idea instead of showing everything at once.

articles.title: CREATORS ARE QUIETLY BECOMING MEDIA CONGLOMERATES
articles.summary: US brands will spend at least $21 billion on creators in 2026, nearly double 2022, while publishers' revenue advantage over creator earnings has collapsed from 44% to roughly 26% over the same span. The biggest names, led by MrBeast's Beast Industries, are restructuring into parent companies spanning chocolate, toys, financial services, and a planned mobile carrier, hiring CEOs pulled from traditional media rather than running a single YouTube channel. The diversification hedges against any one line failing and reduces the key-man risk that makes a business hard to sell, since buyers want a team that can run without its founder.

articles.title: BOWLING ALONE, YES. BUT WATCHING SPORTS IS ANOTHER THING
articles.summary: As traditional institutions decline, sports fandom stands out as one of the few remaining spaces where people consistently interact and build relationships.

articles.title: GAP VERSUS AMERICAN EAGLE: WHO'S WINNING THE DENIM WARS
articles.summary: American Eagle outperforms Gap in conversion and brand lift through celebrity marketing, while Gap's nostalgia strategy delivers weaker results.

articles.summary: Users can order food through Square, Toast, or Uber Eats and compare hotel prices and availability inside Ask Maps.
